text: Could AI training be paused at the chip level? The hardware shown is ordinary electronics, not a working pause system. A Berkeley-led report proposes an international agreement to stop making training-capable chips, then gradually replace existing stocks with hardware designed to run approved models. Training a new model and running one already built are different jobs. The authors argue that hardware controls could make a frontier-training pause more durable. But this is a conditional proposal, not an implemented off-switch. It depends on cooperation, monitoring and suitable replacement chips. Existing AI risks would remain.
